title: Language record (languages/<code>/language.toml)

code.description: wiktextract `lang_code`, and the locale for word segmentation.

name.description: The language's English name, as in the `#Polish` anchors of wiktextract links.

target.description: Target (gloss) language; always `en` for the English Wiktionary dump.

items.description: [letter, plain]: running text may write `letter` as `plain` (`ё` as `е`).

optionalLetters.description: Letters running text may write as another letter. Every form with `letter` is also indexed with `plain`, and compound stems may be written without it.

elision.description: Elided words are written onto the next word with an apostrophe (French `l'homme`, `qu'il`; Italian `dell'anno`), and segmenters keep the two as one word. A word without an entry of its own is split after its first apostrophe when both parts have entries: the word after it comes first, then the elided word, each with its segment. Words with an entry of their own stay whole (`aujourd'hui`, `d'abord`).

historicalStages.description: Historical stages of the language. A sense, form or pronunciation is dropped when its tags contain every tag of a stage. Each stage is a list because wiktextract splits "Middle Polish" into the tags "Middle" and "Polish".

standardPronNotes.description: `note` values on `sounds` that still mean the standard pronunciation; other notes are regional variants, kept only when nothing else exists.

untrustedFormTags.description: Form tags that mark a misparsed table in this language's data; such rows are dropped.

reflexive.description: Senses Wiktionary labels `reflexive with <particle>` become an entry of their own, with the particle before or after the lemma (`after`: Polish `bawić się`, `wyobrażać sobie`). Learners learn these as words of their own.

tags.description: The tags a table's participle row has, all of them (Polish: the masculine singular adjectival participle; German: any participle).

onlyNew.description: Add a declined form only where no other entry has it, so a participle Wiktionary lists as an adjective keeps its forms (German `bestehende` stays `bestehend`'s). Off where those adjectives carry only figurative senses and the verb is needed (Polish `zniszczony` "beat-up" for `zniszczonych` "destroyed").

sharedWithParticiple.description: With `onlyNew`: a form the participle's own adjective or noun has is added to the verb too, since only another word's form blocks it. French `adopté` "male adoptee" has `adoptés`, which is also `adopter`'s, and the noun `arrivée` "arrival" is `arrivé` + `e`, so it is `arriver`'s too, while `plus` the adverb stays out of `plu` (of `plaire`) + `s`.

participleDeclension.description: Adjectival participles decline like adjectives, but verb tables list only one form (`wymagany`, `ausgelegt`). A participle row with all of `tags` that ends in `ending` also gets its stem with each of `endings` as forms of the verb (`wymaganego`, `wymaganej`; `ausgelegte`, `ausgelegten`).

ownEntryForms.description: Form glosses that describe a word a reader meets on its own, so the word keeps an entry with its base's meaning ("passive of використовувати: to use") instead of only linking to the base. Each item is a set of words, all of which must open the gloss before its "of": `passive` matches "passive of" and "adjectival past passive participle of", `active participle` matches "past active participle of". Ukrainian sets them because its participles are also adjectives (`поширений` "widespread"), which a link to the verb would rank behind it.

pointerWords.description: Words that may make up the opening of a gloss that only names another word's form, before "of" and the linked word: `Yang-vowel form of -어서 (-eoseo)`, `topic-marked form of 나 (na)`, `Post-vowel and post-liquid allomorphic form of -으면`. Every word of the opening must be one of these, compared in lower case. wiktextract reads no `form-of` link there, so without this the reader gets the form's name and not its meaning: the sense becomes a link to the word, as a `form-of` sense is.

stressedLemmas.description: Show the lemma with its stress marks: the headword's `canonical` form, when it spells the same word. Lookups still match unstressed text.

headwordGenders.description: With `headwordInflections`, an adjective or determiner also has the genders its headword line gives as forms (Italian `bancario`, feminine `bancaria`, `bancari`, `bancarie`), where Wiktionary often has no page for them or only a noun's (`piccole` "plural of piccola", a small beer). A noun's other gender stays another word (`attore`, `attrice`). Off where most of those forms have pages of their own: a form both reach then opens on the adjective, by dump order (French `journaux` on "daily").

unmarkedStressForms.description: Forms carry stress marks texts don't write: an accented vowel before another letter of the word (Italian tables write `bisógna`, `dàto`; texts `bisogna`, `dato`). Each such form is also indexed without those marks, unless a form with the same tags is written without any (`vuoi` beside the variant `vòi`). An accent on a word's last letter is spelling and stays (`città`, `perché`).

headwordInflections.description: A word without an inflection table has the cases and numbers its headword line gives as its forms: French nouns and adjectives have no tables (`structure`, plural `structures`), and Wiktionary often has no page of its own for a regular plural. Off where headword lines also name other words (German `der` for `CIA`).

verbChainsThroughEntries.description: A verb form's chain of links goes on through a word with entries but no verb entry, by that word's own verb links: French `partie` is "feminine singular of parti", whose entries are an adjective and a noun and whose verb line is "past participle of partir", so `partie` also reaches `partir`. Otherwise a chain stops at any word with an entry. Off where a participle used as an adjective is mostly read as one: the verb it reaches then ranks with the adjective, and often first (German `naheliegende`, Russian `удаленный`).

skippedPos.description: wiktextract parts of speech whose lines are not imported. Japanese `syllable` is a kana's own line ("The hiragana syllable は"), which names no word a reader looks up.

formlessPos.description: wiktextract parts of speech whose inflection tables are not indexed. Japanese `suffix` lines conjugate endings that the analyzer splits off and finds by their base form (`た`, `ます`), and their tables, Classical forms included, spell short words: `な` as a form of `ず`, `は` of the Old Japanese `ふ`.

featureTags.description: This language's wiktextract tags that give a headword feature, besides the shared ones (`masculine`, `perfective`), for a line all of whose senses have the tag: `godan = ["VerbClass", "Godan"]`. They apply to nouns, verbs and adjectives (`-na` on a Japanese な-adjective), not to suffixes, where a tag may mean something else. The value must be one of the feature's values in `packages/core/src/features.ts`.

lemmaSuffixes.description: Head templates whose words a reader learns with something added, by template name: the lemma gets it (`ja-verb-suru` = `する`: the verb on the page `勉強` is `勉強する`, its reading `べんきょうする`), the bare word stays a form, and table forms without the word are dropped (Wiktionary's tables of katakana する-verbs give `し` and `しろ` for `カール`).

import.description: How the importer reads this language's wiktextract data.

verbBracket.description: The rest of a verb phrase goes to the end of the clause (German `tritt morgen in Kraft`).

hyphenWords.description: Some words are hyphen-joined parts (`что-нибудь`), which the segmenter splits; with context the parts are joined back into one word.

reflexive.description: The reflexive pronoun phrases are written with (German `sich` in `sich vorstellen`), which stands for any of `reflexives` in a sentence (`ich stelle mich vor`).

reflexives.description: Reflexive pronouns a phrase's `reflexive` stands for.

negation.description: The particle that negates a verb, where negation changes the case of the verb's object (`не имеет значения` for `иметь значение`).

maxGap.description: Words allowed between a verb and the rest of its phrase.

separableVerbs.description: Separable verbs: the finite verb with its particle at the end of the clause (`fand ... statt` -> `stattfinden`).

clauseConjunctions.description: Conjunctions that end a clause without punctuation, where the verb bracket and separable verbs look for the clause's end.

reflexiveParticles.description: Words that make a verb reflexive (`się` in `bawić się`). In a verb phrase they may stand on either side of the verb, apart from it, though they are no content word (`Dobrze się bawię`).

capitalNouns.description: Nouns are written with a capital letter (German), so a capitalised word of two or more letters inside a sentence ranks entries with a capitalised lemma first (`In wenigen Tagen`: `der Tag` before `tagen`).

nominalizers.description: With `capitalNouns`: words after which a capitalised infinitive is likely the verb used as a noun (`zum Binden`, `das Tragen`), so the verb keeps its place among the capitalised lemmas.

contractions.description: Forms a phrase's last word takes when it merges with the word after it, by form: a preposition with the article (French `du` for `de`, so `à partir du siècle` is `à partir de`; Spanish `del` for `de`), or an elided word written onto the next one, keyed by its apostrophe form, which stands for any word starting with it (`qu'` for `que`: `parce qu'il` is `parce que`).

verbAfter.description: Words a verb follows (subject and object pronouns, the negation): after one, in its clause, a word's one-word verb and auxiliary entries come before its others (French `je passe` opens on `passer`, not the noun `passe`), a verb whose lemma is the word itself after the verbs it is a form of (`dire` before `dit` "called"). With `elision`, an elided word counts in either place: the host of `n'oublie` follows `n'`, and the word after `qu'il` follows `il`.

verbBeforeJoined.description: Words a hyphen joins to the verb before them (French inverted subjects and imperative objects: `dit-il`, `donne-moi`, `vas-y`): before one, a word's verb and auxiliary entries come before its others, as after `verbAfter`.

noVerbAfter.description: Words no verb follows (determiners that are never a pronoun: French `des`, `ces`, `mon`): after one, in its clause, a word's one-word verb entries come after its others (`des mesures` opens on the noun, not `mesurer`).

participleEndings.description: Endings of past participles (French `é`, `i`, `it`). After a word that can be an auxiliary (it has an `AUX` entry), with at most two adverbs between, a word shaped like a past participle of a verb it is a form of shows that verb before its first noun entry, passing no adjective or adverb (`elle est partie`: `partir` before `partie` "part"). Shaped like one: the word, with one of `import.participleDeclension.endings` or nothing taken off, ends in one of these and is itself a form of that verb, so `j'ai envie` keeps the noun (`envi` is no form of `envier`). These hints apply with `context` only, to the word's own entries: a participle after an auxiliary first, then a verb after `verbAfter` or before `verbBeforeJoined`, then `noVerbAfter`.

abbreviationLeads.description: Words that may stand before an abbreviation as part of it (`и` in `и т. д.`).

dictionary.description: The morphological analyzer's dictionary (Lindera): `unidic` or `ipadic` for Japanese, `ko-dic` for Korean, `cc-cedict` for Chinese.

baseFields.description: Which of the dictionary's detail fields hold a morpheme's base forms, looked up in this order (UniDic: 10, the written base form `いる`; 7, the lemma `要る`). None: the morpheme as written (ko-dic, whose reading field is sometimes another word's).

posFields.description: How many of the dictionary's first detail fields are part-of-speech tags, joined with `-` (UniDic: 4, `名詞-普通名詞-一般`; ko-dic: 1, whose later fields are a semantic class and a reading). A tag joined with `+` is a morpheme the dictionary fused of several (ko-dic `VV+EP`, `했`), which has each of those parts of speech.

typeField.description: The detail field that names the morpheme's type (ko-dic: 4).

types.description: The types whose base forms come from `field` (ko-dic: `Inflect`; not `Compound`, a noun whose parts are no base form of it: `한국어`).

field.description: The detail field that lists the parts, each `base/TAG/…`, joined with `+` (ko-dic: 7, `하/XSV/*+았/EP/*`).

fused.description: Morphemes the dictionary fuses of several, whose surface is no base form (ko-dic: `했` is `하` + `았`, `갈` is `가` + `ᆯ`, `예뻐요` is `예쁘` + `어요`): their base forms are their parts', those `baseSpellings` names first, in order (`했`: `하다`, `-았-`), instead of `baseFields`.

pos.description: Parts of speech of the morpheme, as in `join`; of a fused morpheme, of the part.

spellings.description: The base forms, `*` standing for the analyzer's (`*다`, `-*`).

affix.description: A particle or ending: in a fused morpheme, its base forms come after the stem's (`걸` is `거` + `-ㄹ`: `거` first).

baseSpellings.description: How the dictionary spells base forms the analyzer gives otherwise, by part of speech, the first rule that matches: ko-dic gives a verb's stem (`먹`) where Wiktionary lists `먹다` (`*다`), and particles and endings bare where Wiktionary writes them with hyphens (`-에서`, `-었-`).

baseLetters.description: Letters the analyzer writes in base forms otherwise than the dictionary, replaced in them: ko-dic writes a final consonant ending with the jamo that ends a syllable (`ᆯ` in `가` + `ᆯ`), Wiktionary with the letter (`-ㄹ`).

start.description: At a word's start, read with `standIn` in its place, and only when the rest of the word is of `rest` (the pronoun `이` in `이를`, `이는`, read as `그를`, `그는`). Otherwise inside a word, after a letter of it.

standIn.description: With `start`: a morpheme the dictionary has that behaves alike and is as long (`그` for `이`): the word is analyzed with it in its place, and its reading is the morpheme's, its base forms respelled.

rest.description: With `start`: parts of speech the rest of the word must be (particles), as in `join`.

afterFinal.description: Only right after a Hangul syllable that ends in a consonant (`책|이`, not `아이`).

after.description: Inside a word: parts of speech of the morpheme before it, as in `join` (nouns and pronouns: `생각` + `이`, not `같` + `이`).

before.description: Only before a morpheme of these parts of speech (endings: `이` + `에요` is the copula).

as.description: Inside a word: how to read it, the first that fits.

restore.description: Morphemes the analyzer's dictionary lacks: Lindera's ko-dic has no `이` (the subject particle, the copula, the pronoun), and cuts `생각이` as `생|각이`. Inside a word, the word is analyzed again, cut there, and that reading is kept when the dictionary knows more of the word by it: `생각` + `이` (the particle), not `생` + `각이`, but `호랑이` "tiger" as it is. The morpheme's base form is spelled as `baseSpellings` says. At a word's start, see `start`.

pos.description: Parts of speech of the word's last morpheme, as in `join` (ko-dic `ETM`, an adnominal ending).

before.description: Parts of speech the next word must start with, as in `join` (nouns).

recheck.description: Words the analyzer may have misread, which a language with spaces can check against the next word: an adnominal ending must come before a noun, so `우리는 어떤가요` is not `우리다` + `-는` but `우리` + `-는`. A word (a run without spaces) that ends in a morpheme of `pos` and is not followed by a word that starts with one of `before` is analyzed alone, and that reading is kept when it no longer ends so.

stemSuffixes.description: Parts of speech of suffixes that make a verb or adjective of the word before them, as in `join` (ko-dic `XSV`, `XSA`: `공부` + `했어요`): the word is looked up as its head written with the suffix's base forms first (`공부하다`), then by the head's own.

stemForms.description: Spellings of a stem's forms in the dictionary's inflection tables, `*` standing for the stem as the analyzer cuts it: they reach verbs whose forms the stem is part of, when the analyzer's base form misses one. Japanese, the stem itself: `従え` is a form of `従える`, which UniDic reads as `従う`. Korean, the stem with the infinitive ending: a verb whose stem changes (`듣다`: `들어`) is cut as another verb's (`들` of `들다`), and `들어` is a form of both.

readingField.description: Which detail field holds the reading of a morpheme's lemma (UniDic: 6, `ニン` for `人` after a number). Entries with that reading rank first among those the morpheme finds (`人` as にん, not ひと). Katakana and hiragana compare alike.

numbers.description: Parts of speech of numerals, as in `pos` (`名詞-数詞`). A run of them is one number (`1|0` is `10`), shown by one entry or none, and the word after it is read as a counter (`人` "counter for people" in `3人`).

digits.description: The characters for 0 to 9, in order (`〇一二三四五六七八九`).

units.description: The characters for ten, a hundred and a thousand (`十`, `百`, `千`), written without a 1 before them.

myriads.description: The characters for each fourth power of ten from 10,000 on (`万`, `億`, `兆`), written with a 1 before them.

numerals.description: How the language writes a number in characters, to find a number written in digits under its entry (`10` as `十`, `10月` as `十月`).

counters.description: Wiktionary's parts of speech for a counter (`counter`: `人` "counter for number of people"). For the word after a number, entries of these come before its other entries (`年` "years" before `年` "a year").

pos.description: Parts of speech of the morpheme, as the dictionary tags them, each a prefix of its tags joined with `-` (`助動詞`, `動詞-非自立可能`).

surface.description: Only these spellings of it (`て`, `で`).

base.description: Only these base forms of it (`する`).

after.description: Parts of speech of the morpheme before it, as in `pos`; left out, any morpheme with letters.

join.description: Rules that join a morpheme to the word before it: a word is a morpheme and what the rules join to it (`食べ` + `まし` + `た`).

pos.description: Parts of speech the analyzer gives the morpheme, as in `join`.

after.description: Only after a morpheme of these parts of speech, as read by the rules before; left out, after anything.

before.description: Only before a morpheme of these parts of speech; left out, before anything.

pos.description: Its part of speech instead (`助詞-終助詞`).

base.description: Its base form instead (`よ`); left out, it keeps its own.

reread.description: Rules for morphemes the analyzer misreads in a known place, applied in order from the sentence's start, before `join`: `よ` between two nouns is the particle, not the stem of `よい` (`鏡|よ|鏡|よ`). A reread morpheme has no reading.

line.description: The grammar-file line shown for it, by its word (`お…する`).

before.description: Spellings of the morpheme before the slot (`お`, `ご`).

slot.description: Parts of speech of the one morpheme in the slot, as in `join` (`動詞`, `名詞-普通名詞-サ変可能`).

after.description: What follows the slot, its last morpheme written or in its base form (`する`, `になる`, `ください`).

constructions.description: Constructions with a word in them, which no fixed spelling finds: `お` + a verb's stem + `する` is humble (`お待ちします`, `ご案内します`). The run shows `line` first, then the clicked word's entries. Phrases the dictionary spells out come first (`お願いします`).

pos.description: Parts of speech of the ending, as in `join`.

surface.description: Only these spellings of it (`て`, `で`).

label.description: The label on the entries of the piece it ends (`て form`), explained in the language's `labels.toml`.

formEndings.description: Endings that make a form of the piece before them, as a reader takes it: the ending closes that piece's segment, whose entries get `label`, with the ending's own line after them (`並んで`: `並ぶ` [て form] and `て`). What follows starts a segment that runs to the word's end or the next such ending (`並んで|います`, `作って|みました`).

prefixes.description: Parts of speech of morphemes that join the word after them (`接頭辞`: `お` + `茶`).

suffixes.description: Parts of speech of morphemes that make a new word of the word before them (`接尾辞`: `機械` + `屋` "mechanic"). Such a word without an entry of its own is shown by its parts, each with its own entries, not as its head.

spacedWords.description: The language writes a space after each word with its particles and endings (Korean eojeols), so the piece the segmenter gives is a whole word. A headword spelled as it is written, other than a noun, verb or adjective, is that word, even where the analyzer cuts it into a stem and endings: it comes first (`하지만` "but", cut `하` + `-지만`). A word the analyzer reads as a verb with endings is no noun spelled alike (`하지` "summer solstice", for `하` + `-지`). Off for Japanese, written without spaces, where `だったら` after a noun is the copula, not the conjunction.

ranksByPos.description: A word's or part's entries of the parts of speech `upos` gives the analyzer's reading come before its others, which keep their order (Korean `우리` the pronoun "we" before `우리` "cage"; the particle `-는` before the ending). Off for Japanese, whose kana words are ranked by reading instead.

upos.description: The dictionary's parts of speech (a prefix of its tags, as in `pos`) as Universal Dependencies tags (`名詞`: `NOUN`), to tell which entries fit the analyzer's reading of a word.

analyzer.description: A morphological analyzer finds the word around the clicked piece, for a script without spaces whose segmenter cuts words short (`食|べ|ま|した`). With context, the word is returned as `match` and its morphemes as `segments`, each looked up by its base form. Leave the table out for no analyzer.

context.description: What the sentence around a word (`context`) adds to its lookup.

linkers.description: Linking elements between a modifier and the next part, tried in order; "" is a plain join.

nounLinkers.description: Of `linkers`, those that join a modifier to any noun (German `s`, `es`: `Arbeit|s|zeit`), so a modifier that is a noun's lemma scores with them as with a plain join; other linkers mostly mark a plural (`n`, `en`). For compounds of words, not of stems (no `stemEndings`).

stemEndings.description: Endings a modifier drops before its linker, when modifiers are stems rather than words.

adjectiveEndings.description: With `stemEndings`: endings of adjective forms, which a verb form needs to be a compound's head.

compounds.description: Compound splitting, for words without an entry. Leave the table out for no splitting.

labels.description: Grammar features shown as labels next to the headword (`f`, `anim`, `pf`), in this order. Features an article already shows are left out.

articles.description: The article a noun's lemma starts with, by gender (`Ptan`: plural-only nouns), for languages whose learners learn nouns with it (German `der Hund`). Several genders give `der/das Bonbon`. The gender is then not a label.

headword.description: How the headword shows its grammar.

description: A language record, languages/<code>/language.toml. Every key but code, name and target may be left out.
